questions.question: Height of 6 boys M, N, O, P, Q and R is compared. Height of M is less than only Q and O. Height of P is more than R but less than N. Height of no two boys is same. O is the tallest boy among these boys. Height of how many boys is more than N?
questions.solution:
Given that there are 6 boys with different heights: **M, N, O, P, Q,** and **R**.

From the clues, we can deduce the following relationships:

1. Height of **M** is less than only **Q** and **O**.

→ Only O and Q are taller than M, so the partial order is:

→ **O/Q > O/Q > M > _ > _ > _**

2. **O** is the tallest boy among all.

→ **O > Q > M > _ > _ > _**

3. Height of **P** is more than **R** but less than **N**.

→ **N > P > R**

4. Since M is taller than only P and R, **N** must be placed above M.

Combining all these facts gives the final order from tallest to shortest:

→ **O > Q > M > N > P > R**

Thus, the boys taller than **N** are **O, Q,** and **M**.

Hence, the height of **3** boys is more than **N**.

Hence, the correct answer is **"Option 1".**

questions.question: At what time (approximately) (in AM) between 6 AM and 7 AM will the hour and minute hands of the clock overlap?
questions.solution:
At **6 AM**, the **hour hand** is at 6 and the **minute hand** is at 12.

Angle between them at 6:00 = 6 × 300 = 1800

To **overlap**, the **minute hand** must cover this 1800 relative to the **hour hand**.

Relative speed = 60 − 0.50 = 5.50 per minute.

Time taken to **overlap** = 180 ÷ 5.5 = 360/11 minutes.

360/11 = 32.7272... minutes ≈ 33 minutes.

Therefore, the hands will **overlap** at approximately **6:33 AM**.

Hence, the correct answer is “**Option 2**”.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

The angle between the **hour hand** and **minute hand** = |60H - 11M|over 2

For the hands to **overlap**, the angle must be 00.

Here, H = 6.

0 = (60 × 6 − 11 × M) ÷ 2

0 = 360 − 11M

11M = 360

M = 360/11 = 32.72...

M ≈ 33 minutes.

Hence, the correct answer is **6:33**.

questions.question: A clock shows the correct time at 10 AM. The clock gains 3 seconds every 4 minutes. What time (in PM) will it show at 8 PM the same day?
questions.solution:
The clock was set correctly at **10 AM**.

The target time is **8 PM** on the same day.

Total time duration from 10 AM to 8 PM = **10 hours**

Convert the total duration into minutes:

1 hour = 60 minutes

10 hours = 10 × 60 = **600 minutes**

The clock gains **3 seconds** every **4 minutes**.

Number of 4-minute intervals in 600 minutes = 600 / 4 = **150 intervals**

Total gain in 150 intervals = 150 × 3 seconds = **450 seconds**

Convert the total gain from seconds into minutes and seconds:

Gain in minutes = 450 / 60 = **7.5 minutes**

0.5 minutes = 0.5 × 60 = **30 seconds**

So, the total gain is **7 minutes and 30 seconds**.

The time the clock will show at 8 PM = Actual time + Gain

Time shown = 8:00:00 + 0:07:30 = **8:07:30 PM**

Hence, the correct answer is “**Option 2**”.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Rate of gain = 3 seconds / 4 minutes = **0.75 seconds per minute**.

Total minutes elapsed = **600 minutes**.

Total gain = 600 × 0.75 = **450 seconds**.

450 seconds = 450 / 60 minutes = **7 minutes 30 seconds**.

Display time = 8 PM + 7 min 30 sec = **8:07:30**.

Therefore, the correct answer is **8:07:30**.

questions.question: The Chief Justice of India is appointed by:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**President**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Under **Article 124(2)** of the **Constitution of India**, the **President of India** is the constitutional authority empowered to appoint the **Chief Justice of India (CJI)** and every other **Judge of the Supreme Court**.
 
• The appointment follows the **seniority principle**, where the **outgoing Chief Justice** recommends the name of the **senior-most judge** of the Supreme Court to the **Union Ministry of Law and Justice**.
 
• While the **Union Law Minister** forwards the recommendation to the **Prime Minister**, who then advises the **President**, the **President** remains the ultimate appointing authority under their **seal and warrant**.
 
• The **Supreme Court** has established through the **Second Judges Case (1993)** and **Third Judges Case (1998)** that the **President** must act in accordance with the recommendations of the **Collegium**, which consists of the **CJI** and the **four senior-most judges**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Supreme Court of India**:

 
 
• Established under **Part V**, **Chapter IV** (Articles 124 to 147) of the **Constitution**, it serves as the **apex judicial body**.
 
• The **Chief Justice of India** holds office until the age of **65 years**.
 
• The **CJI** administers the oath of office to the **President**, and conversely, the **President** administers the oath to the **CJI**.
 
 
 
• **Removal Procedure**:
 
 
• A **Judge** can only be removed by the **President** following an address by **Parliament** supported by a **special majority** in both houses.
 
• The grounds for removal are limited to **proved misbehaviour** or **incapacity** as per the **Judges (Inquiry) Act, 1968**.

questions.question: The Council of Ministers at the Union level is responsible to
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lok Sabha**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to **Article 75(3)** of the **Constitution of India**, the **Union Council of Ministers** is collectively responsible to the **Lok Sabha** (House of the People).
 
• The principle of **Collective Responsibility** implies that the entire **Ministry** is at the helm of affairs only as long as it enjoys the confidence of the **majority** in the **Lok Sabha**.
 
• If a **No-Confidence Motion** is passed in the **Lok Sabha**, the entire **Council of Ministers**, including those ministers who are members of the **Rajya Sabha**, must resign immediately.
 
• This accountability ensures that the **Executive** remains subservient to the **Legislature**, which represents the direct will of the citizens in a **Parliamentary Democracy**.
 
• The **Council of Ministers** functions as a single unit; therefore, a vote of no confidence against a single minister is effectively a vote against the entire **Cabinet**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **President**:

 
 
• While the **Council of Ministers** is collectively responsible to the **Lok Sabha**, individual ministers hold office during the **pleasure of the President** under **Article 75(2)**. This is known as **Individual Responsibility**.
 
 
 
• **Rajya Sabha**:
 
 
• Although ministers can be chosen from the **Rajya Sabha**, the council is not responsible to this **Upper House**. The **Rajya Sabha** can discuss policies but cannot remove the government through a **No-Confidence Motion**.
 
 
 
• **Supreme Court**:
 
 
• The **Judiciary** performs **Judicial Review** to check the constitutionality of executive actions but does not hold the **Council of Ministers** politically accountable for day-to-day administration.

questions.question: Who was the founder of the Lodi dynasty, the last ruling house of the Delhi Sultanate?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bahlul Lodi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Lodi dynasty** was the fifth and final ruling family of the **Delhi Sultanate**, governing from **1451 to 1526 AD**.
 
• **Bahlul Lodi** (reigned **1451−1489**) founded the dynasty after the abdication of the last **Sayyid ruler**, **Alam Shah**.
 
• He belonged to the **Shahu Khel** clan of the **Pashtun** (Afghan) **Lodi** tribe, making this the first **Afghan dynasty** to rule over Delhi.
 
• During his 38-year reign, he successfully suppressed various rebellions and annexed the **Sharqi dynasty** of **Jaunpur** in **1479**, which significantly expanded his territory.
 
• He is historically noted for his **tribal democratic** approach, where he treated his **Afghan nobles** as peers rather than subordinates, often sitting on the floor with them to ensure their loyalty and cooperation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sikandar Lodi** (**1489−1517**):

 
 
• He was the son of Bahlul Lodi and is regarded as the most powerful ruler of the dynasty.
 
• He founded the city of **Agra** in **1504** and shifted the capital from Delhi to Agra.
 
• He introduced the **Gazz-i-Sikandari**, a standardized unit for land measurement consisting of **32 digits**.
 
 
 
• **Ibrahim Lodi** (**1517−1526**):
 
 
• He was the last Sultan of the Lodi dynasty and the **Delhi Sultanate**.
 
• His autocratic style and insistence on royal supremacy led to conflict with his Afghan nobles, prompting **Daulat Khan Lodi** to invite **Babur** to invade India.
 
• He was defeated and killed in the **First Battle of Panipat** in **1526**, which ended the Sultanate era and established the **Mughal Empire**.

questions.question: The Simon Commission (1927) faced boycott because
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It excluded Indian members.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Simon Commission**, officially known as the **Indian Statutory Commission**, was sent to India in **1928** (constituted in **November 1927**) to review the functioning of the **Government of India Act 1919**.
 
• The commission was headed by **Sir John Simon** and consisted of **seven members** drawn from the British Parliament.
 
• The fundamental reason for the nationwide boycott was that the commission was an **all-white** body, entirely **excluding Indian members**, which was seen as a denial of the right of Indians to participate in deciding their own constitutional future.
 
• Political groups across the spectrum, including the **Indian National Congress** (during the **1927 Madras Session**) and the **All India Muslim League**, resolved to boycott the commission.
 
• Protests were characterized by the slogan **Go Back Simon** and black flag demonstrations upon the commission's arrival in cities like **Bombay** and **Lahore**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Constitutional Demands and Proposals:**

 
 
• **Provincial Autonomy:** While the Simon Commission actually recommended the abolition of **dyarchy** and the implementation of **Provincial Autonomy** in its **1930 report**, this was not the cause of the initial boycott.
 
• **Dominion Status:** The commission notably refrained from mentioning **Dominion Status** as a goal for India, which further aggravated Indian leaders who sought it as a minimum requirement.
 
• **Separate Electorates:** The commission recommended the continuation of **Separate Electorates** for communal representation, a system that remained a point of contention between different political factions.
 
• **Impact on National Movement:** The protests led to the tragic death of **Lala Lajpat Rai** following a **lathi charge** in **Lahore**, which radicalized the Indian youth and accelerated the demand for **Purna Swaraj** (Complete Independence).
 
• **Nehru Report:** In response to the challenge by **Lord Birkenhead** (Secretary of State) that Indians could not draft a constitution, the **Nehru Report (1928)** was prepared by an all-party committee.

• A **Market Economy** is an economic system where the production and pricing of goods and services are determined by the **interactions** of a country's individual citizens and businesses.

• A radical form of socialism that advocates for a **classless society** where all property is **publicly owned**.
 
• It seeks to eliminate the **private sector** entirely, which is the cornerstone of a **market economy**.
 
 
 
• **Feudalism**:
 
 
• A historical social and economic system used in **medieval Europe** based on **land ownership** and **military service**.

questions.question: In aerobic breakdown of pyruvate (in mitochondria), which of the following is formed?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Carbon dioxide + water + energy**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Aerobic respiration** is a high-efficiency metabolic process that utilizes **Oxygen** to break down organic molecules for cellular energy.
 
• The process initiates in the **Cytoplasm** through **Glycolysis**, where a single **Glucose** molecule is converted into two **Pyruvate** molecules.
 
• In the presence of oxygen, **Pyruvate** is transported into the **Mitochondria**, where it undergoes oxidative decarboxylation to become **Acetyl-CoA** before entering the **Krebs Cycle**.
 
• Within the **Mitochondrial Matrix** and the **Inner Mitochondrial Membrane**, the carbon atoms in pyruvate are completely oxidized to form **Carbon dioxide** (CO₂).
 
• The **Electron Transport Chain** (ETC) facilitates the transfer of electrons to oxygen, the final electron acceptor, resulting in the formation of **Water** (H₂O).
 
• This mitochondrial breakdown is the primary source of **ATP** (Adenosine Triphosphate), yielding approximately **30 to 32 ATP** molecules per glucose molecule, which constitutes the **Energy** used for cellular functions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Anaerobic Respiration Pathways**:

 
 
• **Lactic Acid Formation**: This occurs in **Muscle Cells** during vigorous exercise when oxygen levels are depleted. Pyruvate is converted into **Lactic Acid** and energy, which can lead to muscle fatigue.
 
• **Ethanol Fermentation**: Typically observed in **Yeast** and certain bacteria, this anaerobic process converts pyruvate into **Ethanol**, **Carbon dioxide**, and energy. This is a fundamental process in the **Brewing** and **Baking** industries.
 
 
 
• **Mitochondria**:
 
 
• Known as the **Powerhouse of the Cell**, these organelles possess their own **Mitochondrial DNA** and a double-membrane structure.
 
• The inner membrane is folded into **Cristae** to increase the surface area for the enzymes involved in the **ATP synthase** process.

questions.question:
Which of the following is part of the Concurrent List of the Indian Constitution?

I. Forests

II. Banking
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only I**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Forests** were originally part of the **State List** but were moved to the **Concurrent List** (List III) of the **Seventh Schedule** following the **42nd Constitutional Amendment Act of 1976**. This allows both the **Union Parliament** and the **State Legislatures** to enact laws concerning forest conservation and management. ***Hence, statement I is correct.***
 
• **Banking** is a subject of national importance that requires a uniform policy throughout the country. It is explicitly listed under **Entry 45** of the **Union List** (List I) in the **Seventh Schedule**. Therefore, only the **Central Government** has the exclusive power to make laws related to banking operations and the **Reserve Bank of India**. ***Hence, statement II is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Seventh Schedule**: Under **Article 246**, the Constitution classifies legislative powers into three lists to maintain the federal structure of **India**.

 
 
• **Union List (List I)**: Includes subjects like **Defense**, **Foreign Affairs**, **Railways**, and **Atomic Energy**. It currently contains 100 subjects.
 
• **State List (List II)**: Includes subjects like **Police**, **Public Health**, **Agriculture**, and **Local Government**. It currently contains 61 subjects.
 
• **Concurrent List (List III)**: Includes subjects like **Education**, **Forests**, **Marriage and Divorce**, and **Trade Unions**. It currently contains 52 subjects.
 
 
 
• **42nd Amendment Act, 1976**: This landmark amendment transferred five subjects from the **State List** to the **Concurrent List**, namely:
 
 
• **Education**
 
• **Forests**
 
• **Weights and Measures**
 
• **Protection of Wild Animals and Birds**
 
• **Administration of Justice**
 
 
 
• **Residuary Powers**: Subjects not mentioned in any of the three lists fall under **Residuary Powers**, which are vested in the **Union Parliament** as per **Article 248**.

questions.question: In the context of money supply in India, ____ refers to buying and selling of bonds issued by the Government of India in the open market.

The correct answer is __**Open market operation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Open Market Operations (OMO)** are the primary tools used by the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** to regulate the **money supply** and maintain **liquidity** within the Indian economy.
 
• This process involves the purchase and sale of **Government Securities (G-Secs)**, such as **Treasury Bills** and **dated securities**, directly in the open market to or from commercial banks and financial institutions.
 
• When the **RBI** determines that there is excess liquidity (which may lead to high **inflation**), it **sells government bonds**. This action mops up cash from the banking system, thereby reducing the funds available for lending.
 
• Conversely, to boost liquidity and stimulate economic activity, the **RBI purchases bonds** from the market, injecting fresh capital into the banking system and lowering the cost of credit.
 
• **OMOs** serve as a **quantitative instrument** of **monetary policy**, helping the central bank influence **short-term interest rates** and align them with the **Policy Repo Rate**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Moral Suasion**:

 
 
• This is a **qualitative** or **selective credit control** method where the **RBI** uses psychological pressure and persuasion through meetings and circulars to convince banks to comply with its **monetary guidelines**.
 
 
 
• **Margin Requirement**:
 
 
• This refers to the difference between the **market value of security** (collateral) offered for a loan and the actual amount of **credit** granted. It is used to restrict the flow of credit to speculative or unproductive sectors.
 
 
 
• **Evergreening of loans**:
 
 
• It is a banking practice where a lender provides a **new loan** to a borrower to repay an **existing debt**. This is often done to prevent the original loan from being classified as a **Non-Performing Asset (NPA)**.

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Apply the **BODMAS** rule to solve the expression efficiently.

Solve **Of** and **Brackets** first: (27 of 2) = 54 and 18 of 2 = 36.

Next, perform **Division**: 44 ÷ 4 = 11.

Simplify the expression by canceling out +36 and −36: 89 + 33 − 54 + 11 + 0.

Final calculation: 122 − 54 + 11 = 68 + 11 = 79.

**∴ The correct answer is 79.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given Expression:** 89 + 33 − (27 of 2) + 44 ÷ 4 + 18 of 2 − 36

**Formula Used:** **BODMAS** (Bracket, Of, Division, Multiplication, Addition, Subtraction)

⇒ 89 + 33 − 54 + 44 ÷ 4 + 36 − 36 (Solving **Bracket** and **Of** operations)

⇒ 89 + 33 − 54 + 11 + 36 − 36 (Performing **Division**: 44 ÷ 4 = 11)

⇒ 122 − 54 + 11 + 0 (Solving **Addition**: 89 + 33 = 122 and 36 − 36 = 0)

⇒ 68 + 11 (Solving **Subtraction**: 122 − 54 = 68)

⇒ 79

**∴ The correct answer is 79.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

BODMAS Rule

It stands for **Bracket** (), **Of** (multiplication), **Division** (÷), **Multiplication** (×), **Addition** (+), and **Subtraction** (−).

The 'Of' Operator

In simplification, **Of** indicates multiplication and must be calculated before division and regular multiplication.

Left-to-Right Priority

When operations of the same priority (like addition and subtraction) remain, solve them from **left to right** for accuracy.

questions.question: If x = sqrt{169} times sqrt{81} times sqrt{121} , then what is the value of x?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Identify the **unit digit** of each square root: √169 ends in 3, √81 ends in 9, and √121 ends in 1.

Multiply the unit digits: 3 × 9 × 1 = 27.

The final result must have **7** as its unit digit.

Comparing with the options, only **1287** ends with the digit 7.

**∴ The correct answer is 1287.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** x = √169 × √81 × √121

**Formula Used:** Square root calculation and basic multiplication.

⇒ √169 = 13 (since 13 × 13 = 169)

⇒ √81 = 9 (since 9 × 9 = 81)

⇒ √121 = 11 (since 11 × 11 = 121)

⇒ x = 13 × 9 × 11

⇒ x = 117 × 11

⇒ x = 1287

**∴ The correct answer is 1287.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Perfect Squares

A **perfect square** is a number that can be expressed as the product of an integer with itself. For exam speed, memorize squares from 1 to 30.

Multiplication by 11 Shortcut

To multiply a number by 11, such as 117 × 11, write down the last digit (7), add adjacent digits (7+1=8, 1+1=2), and write the first digit (1) to get **1287**.

Square Root Properties

The property √(a × b) = √a × √b allows for the simplification of products involving multiple square roots independently.

questions.question: The area of a rectangle is 54 square cm. The length of the rectangle is 9 cm. What is the ratio of length and breadth of the rectangle?

**Breadth** = **Area** ÷ **Length** = 54 ÷ 9 = 6 cm

Required **Ratio** (Length : Breadth) = 9 : 6 = 3 : 2

**∴ The correct answer is 3 : 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Area** of the **Rectangle** = 54 cm²

**Length** of the **Rectangle** = 9 cm

**Formula Used:**

**Area** of **Rectangle** = **Length** × **Breadth**

**Ratio** = **Length** : **Breadth**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f794674be577a29cc125f0c9219f4dc62bfba0f05ee2781f72d07708d21ff82d.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 54 = 9 × **Breadth**

⇒ **Breadth** = 54 ÷ 9

⇒ **Breadth** = 6 cm

⇒ **Ratio** = **Length** : **Breadth**

⇒ **Ratio** = 9 : 6

⇒ **Ratio** = 3 : 2

**∴ The correct answer is 3 : 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Perimeter of a Rectangle

The total distance around the boundary of a **rectangle** is calculated using the formula: P = 2 × (length + breadth).

Diagonal of a Rectangle

The **diagonal** (d) of a **rectangle** is the distance between opposite vertices: d = √(length² + breadth²).

Properties of Rectangle

A **rectangle** is a **parallelogram** where all four internal angles are right angles (90°) and opposite sides are equal and parallel.

questions.question: What is the smallest 4-digit number that is divisible by 17?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Smallest 4-digit number = **1000**.

Divide 1000 by 17 → 1000 = (17 × 58) + **14** (Remainder).

To find the next multiple: 1000 + (17 − 14) = **1003**.

**∴ The correct answer is 1003.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Divisor = **17**, Required number = **Smallest 4-digit number**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7327edfdadb752731c9b314acaccddeb73b8550b1105ca609906e003d3dd130b.png] 

⇒ Smallest 4-digit number = **1000**

⇒ Divide 1000 by 17:

⇒ 1000 = 17 × **58** + **14**

⇒ The smallest 4-digit number divisible by 17 must be the multiple just after 986.

⇒ Next Multiple = 17 × 59

⇒ 17 × (60 − 1) = 1020 − 17

⇒ Required number = **1003**

**∴ The correct answer is 1003.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Divisibility Rule for 17

To check if a number is divisible by **17**, subtract 5 times the last digit from the remaining truncated number. Repeat if necessary. Example: 1003 → 100 − (5 × 3) = 85, which is 17 × 5.

General Formula for Smallest n-digit Multiplier

Smallest n-digit number divisible by **x** = (Smallest n-digit number) + (**x** − Remainder), where Remainder is obtained by dividing the smallest n-digit number by **x**.

Largest n-digit Multiplier

Largest n-digit number divisible by **x** = (Largest n-digit number) − (Remainder obtained by dividing it by **x**).

questions.question: ((3.452)² - (2.948)²)/(0.504) = ?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Apply the **algebraic identity**: a² − b² = (a + b)(a − b).

Let a = 3.452 and b = 2.948.

Calculate the **difference**: (a − b) = 3.452 − 2.948 = 0.504, which is equal to the **denominator**.

The expression simplifies to (a + b) × (a − b) ÷ (a − b) = a + b.

Required value = 3.452 + 2.948 = 6.4.

**∴ The correct answer is 6.4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Numerator = (3.452)² − (2.948)²

Denominator = 0.504

**Formula Used:**

The **difference of squares** formula: a² − b² = (a + b)(a − b)

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let a = 3.452 and b = 2.948

⇒ a + b = 3.452 + 2.948 = 6.400

⇒ a − b = 3.452 − 2.948 = 0.504

⇒ Numerator = 6.4 × 0.504

⇒ Expression = (6.4 × 0.504) ÷ 0.504

⇒ Expression = 6.4

**∴ The correct answer is 6.4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Difference of Two Squares

The expression a² − b² can always be factored into (a − b)(a + b).

Perfect Square Trinomial (Sum)

The square of a sum is given by (a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b².

Perfect Square Trinomial (Difference)

The square of a difference is given by (a − b)² = a² − 2ab + b².

questions.question: The perimeter of a rectangle is 60 cm. The length of the rectangle is 4 times of its breadth. What is the length (in cm) of its diagonal?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Sum of **Length** (L) and **Breadth** (B) = 60 ÷ 2 = 30 cm.

Ratio L : B = 4 : 1 ⇒ Total 5 units = 30 cm ⇒ 1 unit = 6 cm.

Actual dimensions: L = 24 cm and B = 6 cm.

**Diagonal** = √(24² + 6²) = 6 × √(4² + 1²) = 6√17 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 6√17 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** **Perimeter** of **rectangle** = 60 cm, **Length** (L) = 4 × **Breadth** (B).

**Formula Used:** **Perimeter** = 2(L + B); **Diagonal** = √(L² + B²).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2be06acfc953825093fafecad73bce937d5c259236f77c21ae8a7af6a4af5e6f.png] 

⇒ 2(L + B) = 60

⇒ L + B = 30

⇒ Since L = 4B, 4B + B = 30

⇒ 5B = 30 ⇒ **Breadth** (B) = 6 cm

⇒ **Length** (L) = 4 × 6 = 24 cm

⇒ **Diagonal** = √(24² + 6²)

⇒ **Diagonal** = √(576 + 36) = √612

⇒ **Diagonal** = √(36 × 17) = 6√17 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 6√17 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Diagonal of a Rectangle

The **diagonal** of a **rectangle** forms the hypotenuse of a right-angled triangle with the **length** and **breadth**: d = √(l² + b²).

Area of a Rectangle

The total space occupied by the **rectangle** is given by **Area** = Length × Breadth (l × b).

Pythagorean Triplets

Common sets of integers that satisfy a² + b² = c², such as (3, 4, 5) or (5, 12, 13), help in quick calculation of **diagonals**.

questions.question: Average of 8 numbers is 30. One of these numbers is 20. 20 is replaced with a new number. New average becomes 42. What is that new number?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Net increase in the **average** = 42 − 30 = 12

Total increase in **sum** = Increase in average × Total numbers = 12 × 8 = 96

New **number** = Replaced number + Total increase = 20 + 96 = 116

**∴ The correct answer is 116.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Number of observations = 8

Original **average** = 30

Replaced **number** = 20

New **average** = 42

**Formula Used:**

Total Sum = Average × Number of observations

New Number = New Total Sum − (Original Total Sum − Replaced Number)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8ffbd0d6eeea92ca6925f16e5e722335f3c637aff3aba2af362d6154d3df3747.png] 

⇒ Original **total sum** = 8 × 30 = 240

⇒ Sum of the other **7 numbers** = 240 − 20 = 220

⇒ New **total sum** = 8 × 42 = 336

⇒ New **number** = 336 − 220 = 116

**∴ The correct answer is 116.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Arithmetic Mean

The average or mean is the sum of all values divided by the total count. Formula: Average = (∑xᵢ) ÷ n.

Replacement Rule

When one value is replaced, the change in average is equal to (New Value − Old Value) ÷ Total Count.

Scaling Property

If every number in a data set is increased or decreased by a constant value k, the average also increases or decreases by k.

questions.question: The ratio of two numbers is 3 : 7 and their Highest Common Factor is 5. What are the two numbers?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The **Highest Common Factor (HCF)** is the common multiplier between terms of a **ratio**.

Numbers = (Ratio Parts) × **HCF**

First number = 3 × 5 = 15

Second number = 7 × 5 = 35

**∴ The correct answer is 15, 35.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Ratio** of numbers = 3 : 7

**HCF** = 5

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/32717d262c4f6a7254cb5ca8059f1eac73408153b0bb281e81565d31898d79f8.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the two numbers be 3x and 7x, where x is a **common factor**.

⇒ Since 3 and 7 are **co-prime** (no common factor other than 1), the **HCF** of 3x and 7x is x.

⇒ From the question, HCF = 5, so x = 5.

⇒ First number = 3x = 3 × 5 = 15.

⇒ Second number = 7x = 7 × 5 = 35.

**∴ The correct answer is 15, 35.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Fundamental Relation

For any two numbers, Product of numbers = HCF × LCM.

LCM from Ratio and HCF

If the ratio of two numbers is a : b and their HCF is h, then their Least Common Multiple (LCM) = a × b × h.

Co-prime Numbers

Two numbers are called co-prime if their HCF is 1. All prime numbers are co-prime to each other.

questions.question: Element A is 18 percent by weight in a mixture. How much mixture is required to obtain 90 kg of element A?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In a **mixture**, 18% weight represents the weight of **Element A**.

Given that 18% = 90 kg

⇒ 1% = 90 ÷ 18 = 5 kg

⇒ 100% (Total weight) = 5 × 100 = 500 kg

**∴ The correct answer is 500 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ Weight of **Element A** in the mixture = 90 kg

⇒ Percentage of **Element A** by weight = 18%

**Formula Used:**

⇒ Total Weight = (Weight of component ÷ Percentage of component) × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/74b112b2459b6a3f5378ab622b30e611408b89b204676770daae5ff1c0cb7d67.png] 

**Calculations:**

Let the total weight of the **mixture** be 'W' kg.

⇒ 18% of W = 90

⇒ (18 ÷ 100) × W = 90

⇒ W = (90 × 100) ÷ 18

⇒ W = 5 × 100

⇒ W = 500 kg

**∴ The correct answer is 500 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Percentage to Value Conversion

To find the value of a percentage of a total: Value = (Total × Percentage) ÷ 100.

Finding the Base Value

If x% of a number is 'A', then the number itself (100%) is calculated as (A ÷ x) × 100.

Successive Percentage

If a value increases by a% and then by b%, the net percentage change is given by [a + b + (a × b) ÷ 100]%.

questions.question: An article is sold for a profit of Rs. 50. Profit percentage is 20 percent. What is the cost price of the article?

⇒ 20 = (50 ÷ Cost Price) × 100

Selling Price (SP)

Loss Percentage

When CP is greater than SP, a loss occurs. Loss % = (Loss ÷ CP) × 100, where Loss = CP − SP.

Marked Price (MP)

The price displayed on the article. Discount is always calculated on the MP: SP = MP − Discount.

questions.question: A person sells an article at the profit of 60 percent. Cost price and selling price are increased by 30 percent and 'y' percent respectively. If the new profit percentage is 40 percent, then what is the value of 'y'?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Assume initial **Cost Price (CP)** = 100 → **Initial SP** = 160.

New CP (30% increase) = 130.

New SP with 40% profit = 130 × 1.4 = 182.

Increase in SP (y%) = [(182 − 160) ÷ 160] × 100 = (22 ÷ 160) × 100 = 13.75%.

**∴ The correct answer is 13.75.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Initial **Profit** = 60%, **CP increase** = 30%, New **Profit** = 40%.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c5260907ab4a86f53be0e8569413ef3245524eaa039a2b98ffec72e413610a54.png] 

⇒ Let **Initial CP** = 100

⇒ **Initial SP** = CP + 60% of CP = 100 + 60 = 160

⇒ **New CP** = 100 + 30% of 100 = 130

⇒ **New Profit** = 40%

⇒ **New SP** = 130 + 40% of 130 = 130 + 52 = 182

⇒ Percentage increase in SP (**y**) = [(New SP − Old SP) ÷ Old SP] × 100

⇒ y = [(182 − 160) ÷ 160] × 100

⇒ y = (22 ÷ 160) × 100 = 13.75

**∴ The correct answer is 13.75.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Profit Percentage Formula

Profit % = [(SP − CP) ÷ CP] × 100. It is always calculated on the **Cost Price** unless specified otherwise.

Successive Percentage Change

If a value increases by a% and then by b%, the net change is [a + b + (a × b) ÷ 100] %.

Relation between CP and SP

SP = CP × [(100 + Profit %) ÷ 100] or SP = CP × [(100 − Loss %) ÷ 100].

questions.question: Total length of train A and train B is 600 metres. These trains are running in opposite direction. Total speed of train A and train B is 40 m/s. In how much time (in seconds) these trains will cross each other?

questions.question: A started from point P to reach point Q at the speed of 50 km/hr. At the same time, B started from point Q to reach point P at the speed of 30 km/hr. They met in between at point S. What is the ratio of distances covered by A and B to reach point S?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When two objects start at the **same time** and move towards each other, the **time** (t) taken to meet is **constant** for both.

Since **Distance = Speed × Time**, when time is constant, **Distance ∝ Speed**.

∴ Ratio of distances covered by A and B = Ratio of their speeds = **50 : 30**.

Simplified Ratio = **5 : 3**.

**∴ The correct answer is 5 : 3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Speed of A = **50 km/hr**, Speed of B = **30 km/hr**. Both start simultaneously.

**Formula Used:** Distance = **Speed × Time**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/116ddb630307f30d1f4cb8f1775da04d1156221475770f51c932ef7bf7ceb270.png] 

⇒ Let the time taken by both A and B to meet at point **S** be **t** hours.

⇒ Distance covered by A to reach S = **PS** = SpeedA × t = **50t**

⇒ Distance covered by B to reach S = **QS** = SpeedB × t = **30t**

⇒ Ratio of distances covered = **PS : QS**

⇒ Ratio = 50t : 30t

⇒ Ratio = 50 : 30 = **5 : 3**

**∴ The correct answer is 5 : 3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed in Opposite Direction

When two objects move towards each other, their **Relative Speed** is the sum of their individual speeds (S₁ + S₂).

Constant Distance Relation

If the **distance** is constant, the ratio of speeds is **inversely proportional** to the ratio of time taken (S₁/S₂ = T₂/T₁).

Meeting Time Formula

Time taken to meet = **Total Distance ÷ Relative Speed**. This applies when both start at the same time.

**__Key Points__**

__

• The given sentence is an **interrogative sentence** written in the **Future Indefinite Tense** (Active Voice). It denotes an inquiry about a future action.

• The structure for an **interrogative sentence** in the **Active Voice** (Simple Future) is: **Will/Shall + Subject + Root Form of Verb (V1) + Object?** In the prompt, **the sponsors** is the subject and **the whole team** is the object.

• To convert such a sentence into **Passive Voice**, the structure must change to: **Will/Shall + Object (New Subject) + be + Past Participle (V3) + by + Subject (New Object)?**

• Following this rule, the **object** 'the whole team' is moved to the position of the subject. The **auxiliary verb** 'be' is added before the **past participle** form of the verb 'invite', which is **invited**.

• The original subject 'the sponsors' is placed at the end of the clause, preceded by the preposition **by** to indicate the **agent** of the action.

 **Additional Information__**

• **Rules of Passive Transformation**:

• For **Future Indefinite** sentences, the addition of the word **be** is mandatory to support the **third form of the verb**.

• The **tense** of the sentence must remain consistent during the transformation; only the focus shifts from the **doer** to the **receiver** of the action.

• If the sentence were a declarative statement (e.g., 'The sponsors will invite...'), the passive would be 'The whole team **will be invited**...'.

• Evaluation of Incorrect Options:

• **Option 1** is incorrect because it uses the **first form** of the verb 'invite' and completely omits the required auxiliary **be**.

• **Option 2** is incorrect because it maintains the **Active Voice** structure while simply swapping the positions of the subject and object, which fundamentally alters the **intended meaning**.

• **Option 3** is incorrect as it uses **been**. This auxiliary is exclusively used for **Perfect Tenses** (like Future Perfect: 'will have been invited') and is not used in Simple Future passive structures.

</ul

It was __a once-in-the-lifetime opportunity__ that many would consider invaluable, but very few got the chance to experience.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**a once-in-a-lifetime**__.

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase **once-in-a-lifetime** is a standard **idiomatic expression** and a **compound adjective** used to describe an event that is exceptionally rare, unique, or likely to happen only once.
 
• In the original sentence, the phrase **once-in-the-lifetime** is used. This is grammatically incorrect because the standard idiom requires the **indefinite article** (a) within the hyphenated structure to denote any single lifetime, rather than the **definite article** (the).
 
• Linguistically, the word **once** begins with the vowel letter **o**, but it is phonetically pronounced starting with the **consonant sound** **w** (/wʌns/).
 
• According to **English grammar rules**, the article **a** is used before words that begin with a **consonant sound**, while **an** is reserved for words beginning with a **vowel sound**. Therefore, **a once-in-a-lifetime** is the only phonetically and idiomatically correct choice.

 **Additional Information__**

 
• **Phonetic Article Selection**:
 
 
• The choice between **a** and **an** depends on the **initial sound** of the next word.
 
• Words starting with vowel letters but **consonant sounds** include **a university** (/juː/) and **a one-way street** (/wʌn/).
 
• Words starting with consonant letters but **vowel sounds** include **an hour** (/aʊər/) and **an honor** (/ɒn.ər/).
 
 
 
• **Hyphenation Rules for Compound Adjectives**:
 
 
• A **compound adjective** (like **once-in-a-lifetime**) is a group of words that functions as a single unit to modify a noun (**opportunity**).
 
• These are **hyphenated** when they precede the noun they modify to prevent **ambiguity** and help the reader identify the group as a single descriptive unit.
 
• If the adjective follows the noun (e.g., The opportunity was once in a lifetime), the hyphens are usually omitted.
